title: Assemble a shock-corded antenna mast
instruction: Assemble the green shock-corded mast into one straight pole with every joint fully seated, lay it across the two grey stands, then let go.
context: Field radio and tower installers (O*NET 49-2021.00) put up shock-corded masts and whips; tent poles and deployable booms use the same ferrule joints. The ability: seat the joints of an elastic-linked chain one after another, each pushed past the point where the elastic stops drawing it in. A hinge must first be swung within 3 deg of straight or its spigot cannot enter at all; the cord then draws it in, but the snug ferrule stops it 11.7 to 15 mm short, and a joint left short cracks under load. Each seated joint turns two sections into one rigid piece that is swung and pushed as a unit at the next. Unlike TK-2K8E9N, TK-NSB3C4 and TK-RB5CWP (one rigid part steadied while a single insert is pushed home), the parts are a folded, cord-linked chain worked joint by joint, and the second arm steadying it only enables each push. The finished pole rests in the two-saddle transit cradle where the antenna head is fitted next.
setup: Station table; positions in metres, x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; the table top is at z 0.7475. (1) Mast: three green glass-fibre sections, sRGB (0.20, 0.50, 0.22), 18 mm square tube, 130 mm long, 45 g each, friction 0.5 / 0.45. The base section has a 10 mm black rubber foot, sRGB (0.08, 0.08, 0.08); the top section a 10 mm orange cap, sRGB (0.95, 0.45, 0.08). Each joint is an aluminium ferrule, sRGB (0.78, 0.78, 0.80), 26 mm deep with a 14 mm bore (2 mm walls) on the lower section and a 12 mm square aluminium spigot 26 mm long on the upper one, joined by an internal shock cord: 150 N/m, 0.75 N at home, 4.65 N with the spigot at the mouth. The last 15 mm of each ferrule is a snug fit that holds the spigot until 3 N net acts on it and drags at 2.5 N while it slides, so the cord alone stops a lined-up spigot 11.7 to 15 mm short. A spigot enters only within 3 deg of straight; a bent joint's spigot tip rests on the ferrule's rim; each joint bends up to 70 deg. Start: lying on the table in a zig-zag, base section along y at x 0.36 from its foot at y 0.195 to its ferrule at y 0.065, joint 1 bent 60 deg toward the robot, joint 2 bent 60 deg back so the top section lies parallel to the base section at x 0.222 (y -0.04 to -0.17), both spigots 3.5 mm outside their ferrules. Assembled it is 390 mm long. (2) A transit cradle of two saddle stands, where the antenna head is fitted next: grey anodised aluminium, sRGB (0.45, 0.47, 0.50), fixed to the table at (0.30, -0.30) and (0.30, -0.45), in front of the right arm and past the right end of the mast's line; each a 40 x 24 x 40 mm block with two 6 mm cheeks forming a 28 mm wide, 12 mm deep slot along y whose floor is 40 mm above the table; 0.2 kg each; friction 0.5 / 0.45.
scoring: Every control step from reset, a whole-run record (a linkkit History cleared only by the simulator reset, so pulling a joint apart and starting again never clears what happened) measures each joint's gap at its ferrule mouth (mm) and bend (deg), where the mast's centre line crosses each stand (offset across the slot, tube bottom above the slot floor, offset along the slot), the mast's speed from its pose change between control steps, and each gripper's pad clearance to the mast and speed. A joint is fully seated with a gap of at most 1.0 mm and a bend of at most 1 deg (a feeler gauge at the ferrule mouth). On the stands: at each stand the centre line within 6 mm of the slot centre, the tube bottom -2 to +4.5 mm from the slot floor (a square tube tipped onto an edge sits up to 3.7 mm high, one on the cheek tops 12 mm), and the nearest centre-line point within 12 mm of the stand along the slot. Ladder: 0.25 = one joint fully seated at some time; 0.5 = both joints fully seated at the same time, at some time; 0.75 = at the end both joints fully seated, the mast on both stands and still (under 5 mm/s); 1.0 = 0.75 held for 1 s, plus the release gate: every pad point of both grippers at least 30 mm from the mast and both grippers under 5 mm/s for the last 1 s. Success (1.0) must hold 1 s.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Pull each joint apart and lay the mast back in its zig-zag on the taped outline: base section along its line with the foot on its mark, joint 1 bent 60 deg toward the robot, joint 2 bent 60 deg back so the top section lies parallel to the base section, each spigot tip resting on its ferrule's rim (a 60 deg template card at each joint). The stands are fixed on taped outlines and need no reset.
fidelity: Square tubes stand in for round ones and the joints bend only in the table plane. The cord is a linear spring along each joint. The snug fit is stick-slip on that slide (holds until 3 N, drags 2.5 N while sliding). Joint limits switched each step stand in for the spigot: it enters only within 3 deg of straight, rests on the rim when bent, and once in holds the joint straight. Light cord and fit forces suit the YAM's soft wrist (about 0.2 N/mm).
